reasoning_summary: The setup matches the question. Re = 0.15*0.01/1.5e-5 = 100, which equals the configured 100. The force references (magUInf 0.15, lRef 0.01, Aref 0.0001, rho 1.2) are consistent with the geometry and fluid. The inlet is measured uniform (ux_nonuniformity 0.0, uy_max_abs 0.0).

The domain is effectively unbounded: blockage is 0.0125, with 30D upstream, 50D downstream and 40D half-height. The boundary conditions are standard and the run is stable. Max Courant is 0.73373, mass imbalance is 8.3333e-11, checkMesh passed, and max non-orthogonality is 43.313 deg.

The temporal resolution is good: 613.51 steps per shedding period with backward time stepping and linearUpwind convection. The run is clearly oscillating and has 5 stationary cycles. The lift amplitude is consistent with the RMS lift: 0.31635 against 0.22362*sqrt(2).

Drag looks statistically stable. The stationary-window mean Cd is 1.3266, with a 95% CI of 0.0058205 (about 0.4%), drift of 0.010388 and half-window difference of 0.0055829. All of these are well below the 3% tolerance. The setup-reported Cd of 1.3196 differs from the window value by about 0.5%.

Strouhal estimates agree with each other. The period-based value is 0.163, the FFT value is 0.16316, and the setup-reported value is 0.16144, so the spread is about 1%. The FFT frequency resolution of 0.016669 is coarse, but the 5-cycle period count from 613.51 steps per period gives a much finer estimate that matches the FFT.

Residual risks: there is no mesh or domain refinement study. The mesh is moderately coarse in the wake (111 streamwise cells, last cell 1.0209 D), and the stationary-window start is the MSER cap at 27.88. The near-cylinder resolution is fine (160 cells around, first cell 0.005 D), and Cd and St are mostly set near the body. The recorded drift is about 1%, so I judge these risks small against the 3% tolerance, but not fully ruled out. This is why confidence is medium.
